known_limitation: The lookup mutates the context node's output in place (adapter.py: reground_lookup appends novel to context asked and sets rounds=1), so the persisted context record shows the lookup's questions and rounds=1 -- a later write visibly rewriting an earlier phase's record. Same pre-existing shape as domain_review flipping implement.green. Fix belongs to 097 (ledger serialised per node completion).
questions_for_advisor: research_gaps findings are NOT attributable per blocker: the adapter counts findings per round only. The D37 falsifier therefore counts findings per round and states that it cannot attribute them.

Wiring chosen: a loop declared exactly like build_loop: '- id: regrounding_loop / kind: ai / body: [plan, reground_context, reground_lookup] / until: reground_context.passed == false / max_iterations: 2 / depends_on: [context]' with no on_exhausted (see deviations), no tier/specialist/prompt/schema/max_tokens. A linear chain runs each node id once so plan would run once; no second id would do since downstream reads plan.*.

Budget re-derivation: worst case on the re-grounding path is one extra plan pass (architecture tier) plus one bundled search lookup (research_gaps at search_max_tokens, one request). No scenario max_calls or timeout changes: convergence scenarios declare max_calls 40 and the measured happy-path call count is unchanged (10/17 README table holds; test_docs green), so headroom exceeds the worst case by an order of magnitude. For time: no committed trace exercises the loop yet (all 13 night traces predate the edge), so no timing claim is made -- the loop adds at most one plan latency plus one lookup latency.
